After being released from the hospital, Jarrell was brought to court in a wheelchair, where the following charges were read. One count of first-degree murder, one count of attempted murder of a peace officer, one count of possession of a stolen firearm, and one count of unlawful use of a weapon by a felon. Jarrell is being held without bond as his case moves to trial. Notably, he has two prior felony convictions for a crime. aggravated battery against law enforcement, which prohibited him from owning a firearm. Reports show he stole the gun from his sister, after an altercation with his father. She reported the missing gun to Chicago Police five days before the shooting. Gerald faces a minimum of 20 years in prison without probation, and a maximum of life without parole. He will not face the death penalty, as the incident occurred in Illinois.
